title: Tropical Storm Lala forms near Hawaii, hurricane watch issued for the Big Island
facts: Tropical Storm Lala formed in the Pacific Ocean on Thursday, August 13, 2026.
The National Hurricane Center issued a hurricane watch for the Big Island of Hawaii.
The National Hurricane Center is headquartered in Miami.
Tropical Storm Lala was located approximately 680 miles east-southeast of Hilo, Hawaii.
Tropical Storm Lala registered maximum sustained winds of 40 mph while moving west.
Forecasters projected Tropical Storm Lala would bring rain to Hawaii starting late Friday.
Forecasters warned that wind speeds on the windward sides of hills and mountains can be up to 30% stronger than near-surface winds.
The forecast track showed Tropical Storm Lala passing near or just south of the Big Island on Saturday.
Tropical Storm Lala is forecast to pass south of the smaller Hawaiian islands over the weekend.
Forecasters estimated rainfall totals between 5 and 10 inches for the Hawaiian Islands from Tropical Storm Lala.
Peak rainfall totals from Tropical Storm Lala were forecast to potentially reach up to 20 inches.
The National Weather Service warned of life-threatening flooding and mudslides in steep terrain from the rainfall.
Tropical Storm Hernan formed in the Pacific Ocean about 1,460 miles west of the southern tip of Baja California.
Tropical Storm Hernan formed on Thursday, August 13, 2026.
Forecasters stated that Tropical Storm Hernan is not expected to threaten land.
